fragments.text: The third even broader aspect linking AI ethics and information is access to AI knowledge itself. And the moment AI knowledge, like many advanced sciences, is largely confined to the labs of developed countries and large multinationals and some startups, but mostly those are also based in developed countries. Knowledge produced by these entities isn't automatically shared with everyone. And while that could potentially be tolerable in disciplines that only affect one domain of life, AI has become so intertwined in almost all aspects of our daily lives that any withholding of information or exclusivity of access to knowledge will inevitably have an adverse and immediate effect, especially on marginalized and underrepresented groups, be those ethnically graphical, gender-based people,
